title: 13 one-tap time tracker apps compared — Tap Time Tracker
description: TickTappy, aTimeLogger, Simple Time Tracker, Timeular and 9 more one-tap time trackers, ranked by how close they are to Tap Time Tracker.
heading: One-tap time tracker apps compared
intro: Tap Time Tracker works like a chess clock: tap an activity to start it, tap another to switch, only one runs at a time, and past times can be corrected. These apps work in the same or a similar way. They are ordered from most to least similar.

best.q: Which app is most like Tap Time Tracker?
best.a: It depends on your device. On iPhone, iPad and Mac, TickTappy is the closest: tap-to-switch tags and timers started in the past. aTimeLogger is the long-standing one-tap logger for iOS, and Simple Time Tracker the open-source pick for Android. None of them runs in a browser.

different.q: What does Tap Time Tracker do that they don’t?

compare.a: Each row shows where the app runs, what it shares with Tap Time Tracker and how it differs.

takeaway.lead: In short: none of them combines all of the following:
takeaway.web: a web page that runs anywhere and installs as an app that works offline
takeaway.backdate: “active since…” backdating that takes the time away from other activities
takeaway.offline: storage that stays on the device, with no account

t1.platform: iPhone, iPad, Mac, Watch; free + premium (sync)
t1.similar: Colored tag buttons: tap to start, tap again to stop, starting another tag stops the running one. Start a timer in the past (e.g. 30 min ago), quick time adjustment after start/stop, editing past entries, archiving tags without losing history, day/week summaries. Offline, no account.
t1.differences: Apple only; not a web page; no wall-display mode

t2.similar: Starts and stops an activity with one tap; pause/resume; optional simultaneous activities; reports.
t2.differences: Native app; several activities can run at once (optional); not a kiosk layout

t3.similar: Starts activities with one click from a grid of activity buttons; record history, statistics, backups, home-screen widgets; a record can be divided and its activity changed.
t3.differences: Android only; not a web app

t4.similar: One tap to start, stop or switch activities; the start time of a running entry can be moved.
t4.differences: Apple only; segmented entries can’t be adjusted after a while

t5.similar: Starts and stops task tracking with one tap; reports per task.
t5.differences: Native app; switching and pause behavior not described

t6.platform: Physical 8- or 12-sided tracker die + app; subscription
t6.similar: Same “one active activity” idea as a physical device: flip the die to switch activity, turn it off or double-tap to stop. Forgotten time is fixed in a calendar-like editor.
t6.differences: Needs hardware; cloud account; no on-screen buttons (comparison)

t7.platform: Web, on a shared device; free feature of Clockify
t7.similar: A shared-device / kiosk web page: people clock in and switch projects or tasks and breaks; reports in Clockify (help).
t7.differences: Built for teams (PIN/QR sign-in); cloud only; no per-activity button board

t8.platform: Web app; open source (GPL-3.0), self-host or hosted
t8.similar: Web-based, with an interactive timeline for editing records; tags instead of projects; daily/weekly/monthly targets; reports (PDF/CSV); Pomodoro mode (overview).
t8.differences: Python server; not a big-button touch board; no tap-to-switch

t9.similar: Saved timers started with one click; editing and splitting entries; in Toggl you drag a block to change its start or stop time (guide).
t9.differences: Cloud account; desktop/phone UI; free tier is limited

t10.platform: Static web page (vanilla JS, Bootstrap), localStorage mode
t10.similar: Closest tech stack: plain JS, browser storage, one card per activity with start/stop and an hours total.
t10.differences: No automatic switching, per-day totals view or backdating

t11.differences: A start/stop/lap stopwatch, not an activity board

t12.similar: General time tracking with projects/tasks, timers and reports; self-hostable or local-first (comparison).
t12.differences: Project/billing oriented; no one-tap activity board

t13.similar: The chess-clock interaction Tap Time Tracker is modelled on: big buttons, one tap hands the clock to the other side.
t13.differences: Two players, counts down, no logging, totals or history

sources: Researched in October 2026. Descriptions come from each app’s own listing or docs, plus third-party summaries; nothing was installed or tested.
